root_cause.text: The `nfsd` NFSv4 grace-period teardown path lacked synchronization between `write_v4_end_grace()`/`nfsd4_end_grace()` and server shutdown, so a forced grace-end write could reschedule laundromat work or access `nfsd_net` state after it had already been freed.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says “Writing to v4_end_grace can race with server shutdown and result in memory being accessed after it was freed - reclaim_str_hashtbl in particularly,” and the patch adds `client_tracking_active` protected by `nn->client_lock`, sets it false before `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&nn->laundromat_work)`, and makes `nfsd4_force_end_grace()` return false unless `client_tracking_active` is set before calling `mod_delayed_work()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `nfsd` NFSv4 grace-period teardown path lacked synchronization between `write_v4_end_grace()`/`nfsd4_end_grace()` and server shutdown, so a forced grace-end write could reschedule laundromat work or access `nfsd_net` state after it had already been freed.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE says “Writing to v4_end_grace can race with server shutdown and result in memory being accessed after it was freed - reclaim_str_hashtbl in particularly,” and the patch adds `client_tracking_active` protected by `nn->client_lock`, sets it false before `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&nn->laundromat_work)`, and makes `nfsd4_force_end_grace()` return false unless `client_tracking_active` is set before calling `mod_delayed_work()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add per-net NFSd state flags to track forced grace ending and client tracking status.
intent_record.what: Two new boolean fields, `grace_end_forced` and `client_tracking_active`, were added to `struct nfsd_net` immediately after the existing `grace_ended` member.
intent_record.how: This expands the per-network NFS server state to record whether grace termination was forced and whether client tracking is currently active, enabling later code to make runtime decisions based on these new flags.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make nfsd4_end_grace a file-local helper by changing its declaration to static.
intent_record.what: The forward declaration of nfsd4_end_grace(struct nfsd_net *nn) was changed from non-static to static.
intent_record.how: This limits the visibility of nfsd4_end_grace to the current translation unit, matching an internal helper function declaration and preventing external linkage use.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make `nfsd4_end_grace()` a file-local helper by marking it static.
intent_record.what: The function declaration for `nfsd4_end_grace(struct nfsd_net *nn)` was changed from `void` with external linkage to `static void`, limiting its visibility to the translation unit.
intent_record.how: This does not change the function's runtime behavior, but it prevents the symbol from being exported or referenced from other source files, enforcing file-local scope and reducing external coupling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to forcibly end NFSv4 grace by scheduling immediate laundromat work when grace termination needs to be expedited.
intent_record.what: A new function, `nfsd4_force_end_grace(struct nfsd_net *nn)`, was added. It is documented with a kernel-doc comment and implements an early return if `nn->client_tracking_ops` is absent. It then takes `nn->client_lock`, checks `nn->grace_ended` and `nn->client_tracking_active`, returns false if either indicates no action is needed, otherwise sets `nn->grace_end_forced` to true with `WRITE_ONCE()`, schedules `nn->laundromat_work` immediately via `mod_delayed_work(laundry_wq, ..., 0)`, unlocks, and returns true.
intent_record.how: This enables the NFS server to forcibly bypass the normal grace-period completion path and trigger the laundromat work item immediately, causing grace-period termination to be scheduled without waiting for the usual conditions to complete. If client tracking is unavailable or the grace period is already ended/inactive, the function does nothing and reports failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early forced-grace-end check so reclaiming stops immediately when `grace_end_forced` is set.
intent_record.what: The function `clients_still_reclaiming(struct nfsd_net *nn)` was modified to add an early check for `READ_ONCE(nn->grace_end_forced)`, and if that flag is set the function now returns `false` immediately before evaluating the existing reclaim-progress conditions.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes the server to treat reclaiming as complete whenever `grace_end_forced` has been set, bypassing the normal logic that waits for clients to finish reclaiming during the grace period. This can end reclaim handling earlier than before when the forced-grace-end condition is active.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize additional NFS4 state flags to false during net namespace setup to ensure correct default grace and client-tracking behavior.
intent_record.what: Two new fields in the NFS4 per-net state initialization are explicitly set to false: nn->grace_end_forced and nn->client_tracking_active, added immediately after nn->grace_ended is initialized.
intent_record.how: This ensures newly created network namespace NFS state starts with these flags in a known disabled state, preventing them from retaining any stale or undefined value and affecting grace-period or client-tracking behavior at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Enable client tracking before laundromat activity during NFSv4 net startup to avoid races with uninitialized tracking state.
intent_record.what: In nfs4_state_start_net(), after locks_start_grace() and nfsd4_client_tracking_init(), the code now acquires nn->client_lock, sets nn->client_tracking_active to true, and releases the lock before the existing grace-period logic continues.
intent_record.how: This makes client tracking explicitly active earlier in the network state startup sequence, allowing the laundromat to safely operate only after the tracking infrastructure is initialized and preventing it from running against an uninitialized or inactive client-tracking state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable NFS client tracking during network namespace shutdown to prevent stale tracking state from persisting.
intent_record.what: In nfs4_state_shutdown_net(), the code now acquires nn->client_lock and sets nn->client_tracking_active to false before releasing the lock, inserted after cancel_work_sync(&nn->nfsd_shrinker_work) and before cancel_delayed_work_sync(&nn->laundromat_work).
intent_record.how: At shutdown time, this explicitly disables client tracking under the protection of the client lock, preventing other paths from seeing client tracking as still active while the network namespace is being torn down.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the new helper to validate and force ending NFSv4 grace, returning `-EBUSY` when the transition is not allowed.
intent_record.what: In `write_v4_end_grace()`, the code that handled the `'Y'`, `'y'`, and `'1'` inputs was changed from directly checking `!nn->nfsd_serv` and then calling `nfsd4_end_grace(nn)` to instead calling `nfsd4_force_end_grace(nn)` and returning `-EBUSY` if that helper fails. The explicit `nfsd4_end_grace(nn)` call was removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now delegates the decision of whether grace can be ended to `nfsd4_force_end_grace()`, which likely performs additional state validation or forces the transition only when allowed. If the helper indicates the operation cannot proceed, the write returns `-EBUSY`; otherwise, the grace-period termination proceeds and tracing still occurs. This changes the behavior from a simple server-existence check to a more robust, centralized gating path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename the grace-period समाप्ति helper to a forced variant and return success status to support controlled grace-period termination.
intent_record.what: The function declaration under the "grace period management" comment was changed from `void nfsd4_end_grace(struct nfsd_net *nn);` to `bool nfsd4_force_end_grace(struct nfsd_net *nn);`, including a name change and a return type change from `void` to `bool`.
intent_record.how: This changes the interface so callers can request a forced end to the grace period and receive a boolean result indicating whether that action succeeded or had an effect, rather than invoking a void routine with no status feedback.

grouping_result.intent: Add per-net NFSd state flags to track forced grace ending and client tracking status.
Make `nfsd4_end_grace()` a file-local helper by marking it static.
Rename the grace-period समाप्ति helper to a forced variant and return success status to support controlled grace-period termination.
Initialize additional NFS4 state flags to false during net namespace setup to ensure correct default grace and client-tracking behavior.
Enable client tracking before laundromat activity during NFSv4 net startup to avoid races with uninitialized tracking state.
Disable NFS client tracking during network namespace shutdown to prevent stale tracking state from persisting.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make nfsd4_end_grace() a file-local helper by marking it static.
Introduce and use a forced grace-period termination path for NFSv4, including renaming the helper and ensuring reclaim handling stops immediately when forced termination is active.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds per-net NFSd state flags specifically to track forced grace ending and client tracking status, which directly relates to coordinating grace-period teardown with shutdown and preventing unsafe accesses or rescheduling after teardown.

The change only makes `nfsd4_end_grace()` file-local by marking it static. It does not address the synchronization/shutdown race in the grace-period teardown path, nor the possibility of rescheduling laundromat work or accessing freed `nfsd_net` state.

The changes directly concern forced NFSv4 grace-period termination, including rescheduling laundromat work and stopping reclaim processing when grace end is forced. That matches the root cause around unsafe interaction between forced grace-end handling and server shutdown / freed nfsd_net state.

The change only initializes NFSv4 state flags during net namespace setup. It does not address the teardown/shutdown synchronization issue between write_v4_end_grace()/nfsd4_end_grace() and freeing nfsd_net, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.

The change is about startup ordering for client tracking and laundromat activity, preventing use of uninitialized state. The root cause concerns shutdown/grace-end synchronization and avoiding use-after-free/rescheduling after nfsd_net teardown, which is a different race.

The change disables NFS client tracking during network namespace shutdown to avoid stale state, but the root cause is a race in nfsd grace-period teardown where write_v4_end_grace()/nfsd4_end_grace() could run after or during shutdown and touch freed nfsd_net state. This hunk does not address that synchronization or teardown race.

The change targets the NFSv4 grace-period end path and adds validation/forced-ending logic with -EBUSY when the transition is unsafe, which directly relates to the teardown/shutdown synchronization issue described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct forced grace-end call from the sysctl write path. Before the fix it lacked synchronization with shutdown, so it could run while server teardown was already freeing nfsd_net state, leading to races and use-after-free or rescheduling laundromat work after shutdown.

This precedes the unsynchronized grace-ending action in the write path and indicates the exact code path that can be triggered during shutdown. It is part of the vulnerable sequence that allowed forced grace termination to proceed without coordinating with server teardown.

This condition shows the pre-fix reclaim-handling logic that could continue evaluating and scheduling grace-period progress based on nfsd_net state. Without an early forced-end check, this code path could still run after shutdown had begun.

This line is part of the reclaim-completion check that the forced-end fix interrupts. In the vulnerable version, this state-dependent logic could still be reached and act on nn after teardown, contributing to the race with freed nfsd_net state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the sysctl write-path trace immediately before the forced NFSv4 grace-end action. In the vulnerable code, it could proceed during server shutdown without synchronization, allowing the subsequent grace-end transition to race with teardown and freed nfsd_net state.

This is the direct forced grace-end call from the write path. Before the fix it lacked coordination with server shutdown, so it could reschedule laundromat work or access nfsd_net after that state had already been freed.

This condition begins the reclaim-completion path that depended on nfsd_net state. Without an early forced-grace-end check, this logic could continue running during or after shutdown, contributing to the race with freed nfsd_net data.

This is part of the state check that the fix short-circuits when grace end is forced. In the vulnerable version, it could still evaluate and act on nn after teardown had begun, exposing the shutdown race.
